name: CoreWeave GB300 NVL72, MLPerf Inference v6.1 Server: Llama 2 70B across a full 72-GPU rack (18 nodes) under the Server latency constraint
unit: output tokens/s (aggregate across all 72 GPUs, harness 'Completed tokens per second')
methodology: AGGREGATE. MLPerf Inference v6.1 Closed division, Datacenter suite, SERVER scenario at RACK scale, GB300 generation. LOADS: target_qps 0.5 Poisson arrivals, min_duration 120000 ms, min_query_count 100, compiled-in per-query TTFT/TPOT 99th-percentile bounds, 'Performance constraints satisfied : Yes'. Batch size not a fixed published number. Completed samples per second 3464.52. Model shape TOKENS_PER_SAMPLE 267.0. POWER: has_power=False, design_power_watts=null, no declared cap, no cooling configuration. OMITTED BY SOURCE: replica/TP layout, fabric, KV dtype, concurrency, clock state.
notes: Second-largest Llama result in v6.1. Note the rack-scale Server discount is LARGER here than on GB200: 1136100 Offline to 944902.14 Server is -16.8%, against GB200's +1.9% in the other direction. Same submitters, same harness, same scenario pair, adjacent hardware generations - so the sign and size of the Offline-vs-Server relationship is not a stable property of either the platform or the scenario. It is a property of the load shape at that particular scale point, and it is exactly why an MLPerf comparison that does not state the scenario is not a comparison.
